#WATCH | India's cheetah conservation programme records another milestone as a two-and-a-half-year-old female cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs in the wild.

Identified as KOMG 3, the cheetah is the first female from Botswana to give birth in India. She spent more than four months in the wild before delivering the cubs under natural conditions.

With the latest births, India's cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 born in the country, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced on November 20.

This is only the second recorded birth in the wild since Project Cheetah was launched in 2022. The previous instance was in April 2026, when an India-born female cheetah gave birth to four cubs at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.

India's cheetah reintroduction programme began in September 2022, after the species was declared extinct in the country in 1952. Kuno National Park has been the primary site for the programme.

Yadav credited project managers, veterinarians and frontline forest staff for their role in the conservation effort.

IIFL Finance Ltd – Q2 & H1FY27 | Concall Insights

Financial Performance & FY27 Guidance
•Q2 AUM grew 38% YoY to ₹1,24,268 Cr, while PAT surged 93% YoY to ₹805 Cr.
•H1 annualized ROA stood at 3.1% and ROE at 20.1%.
•Management reiterated ~25% FY27 AUM and profit growth guidance, with potential outperformance.
•Medium-term consolidated ROE target remains above 20%.

Gold Loans – Primary Growth Engine
•Gold loans constitute ~53% of consolidated AUM and 93% of standalone AUM.
•Strong customer acquisition, higher pledged gold tonnage and improving branch productivity driving growth.
•Management expects strong H2 growth momentum, assuming broadly stable gold prices.
•Standalone AUM grew 11% QoQ to ₹70,382 Cr, supported primarily by gold lending.

Home Finance – Growth Acceleration
•Home Finance AUM reached ₹43,070 Cr, growing 4% QoQ.
•Management reiterated 18–20% FY27 AUM growth guidance, supported by accelerating disbursements.
•Affordable housing disbursements nearly doubled QoQ from ~₹400 Cr to ₹790 Cr.
•Higher-yield affordable housing loans and operating leverage expected to improve profitability.
•Management targets 16–18% Home Finance ROE in FY28.

Microfinance – Recovery Visibility
•Samasta AUM remained stable at ₹10,816 Cr, while PAT increased 13% QoQ to ₹69 Cr.
•Gross NPA improved 46 bps QoQ to 2.82%, reflecting better collections.
•Monthly disbursements expected to increase from ~₹550 Cr in September to ~₹1,000 Cr by February–March 2027.
•Management expects gradual growth recovery in H2 FY27 while maintaining conservative underwriting.

Co-Lending & Operating Leverage
•Off-book AUM stands at ₹42,796 Cr, representing 34% of consolidated AUM, supported by 18 banking partners.
•Increasing co-lending enables growth with lower balance-sheet capital requirements.
•Operating expenses declined to 3.3% of average AUM from a peak of 4%.
•AI-enabled processes have demonstrated ~30% productivity improvement in selected workflows, supporting further cost efficiencies.

Funding, Asset Quality & Risks
•Group liquidity stood at ₹13,805 Cr, with consolidated capital adequacy of 23.5%.
•Management evaluating 10–20% equity dilution, potentially during Q3 FY27, to support standalone growth.
•Consolidated GNPA improved to 1.48%, while NNPA stood at 0.87%.
•Potential insurance commission regulation could affect group profitability; management indicated an estimated ~5% PBT impact, subject to final regulations.

Key Takeaway
•Future earnings growth visibility driven by strong gold loan momentum, 18–20% Home Finance AUM growth guidance, microfinance recovery, co-lending expansion and improving operating leverage.
•Key monitorables: Gold price volatility, equity dilution, standalone capital adequacy, insurance commission regulations, Home Finance ROE improvement and credit costs.

Fairfax நிறுவனம் IIFL Capital பங்குகளை ₹350 விலையில் வாங்கி இப்போது 44.08% stake உடன் promoter ஆகிவிட்டார்கள். அதே நேரத்தில் நீங்க கவனிக்க வேண்டியது, IIFL Group founder மற்றும் மற்ற promoters தங்கள் பங்குகளை விற்று வெளியேறுகிறார்கள்.

ஒரு நிறுவனம் வளரும்போது அதன் நிஜமான founders கையில் இருக்கும் 25.80% பங்குகள் 11.85% ஆகக் குறைவதை பார்க்கும்போது ஒன்று மட்டும் தெளிவாகிறது. Business நல்ல நிலையில் இருக்கும்போதே அதற்கான சரியான விலையைப் பெற்று வெளியேறுவது ஒரு தனி கலை. ₹1,540 கோடி மதிப்பிலான இந்த deal நடந்த அன்றே சந்தையில் பங்கு விலை 5.35% குறைந்து ₹334.20க்கு வந்துள்ளது.

பெரிய நிறுவனங்கள் நுழையும்போது ஒரு சலசலப்பு இருக்கும். ஆனால் நீண்ட கால அடிப்படையில் பார்த்தால், ஒரு நிறுவனத்தின் கட்டுப்பாடு யாரிடம் இருக்கிறது என்பதுதான் அதன் போக்கை தீர்மானிக்கும். நீங்கள் ஒரு நிறுவனத்தில் முதலீடு செய்யும்போது அதன் founder வெளியேறுகிறாரா அல்லது பங்குகளை உயர்த்துகிறாரா என்பதை மட்டும் பாருங்கள். அதுதான் உண்மையான signal.

The Heavy Industries Ministry today gave letters of intent to four companies under its ₹7,280 crore rare earth magnet scheme: Coal India, ReNew, Prozeal Green Energy and Midwest Energy.

Coal India's exchange filing this evening has the details:
• Partner: NFTDC, a non-ferrous materials research centre
• Plant: 1,200 tonnes a year of NdFeB magnets, set up through an SPV
• Timeline: 2 years to build, then 5 years of operation
• CIL's bid was ranked L2 (second)

Why it matters: these magnets sit inside EV motors, wind turbines, electronics and defence kit. India makes almost none and imports nearly all of them. China's export curbs last year showed how risky that is.

The scheme's target is 6,000 tonnes a year. Coal India's plant alone would be about one-fifth of it.

My read: for a company of Coal India's size, this is small money for now. The real signal is direction. A coal miner is building a second leg outside coal.

What to watch: an LoI is not the final award. Each firm must still submit performance security and meet compliances before the letter of award. Raw material is the other bottleneck, since IREL's oxide capacity today supports only about 1,200 tonnes of magnets a year.

Canadian investment group Fairfax Financial Holdings has become the controlling shareholder of India's IIFL Capital following an open-offer process and additional share purchases.

For a moment, if you sideline Coal India and look at RARE EARTH PERMANENT MAGNET MANUFACTURING.

What can we think about?

If you map the complete rare-earth permanent magnet value chain, there are 3 layers.

Upstream – Rare earth ore mining, mineral processing and separation, NdPr oxide production and the availability and processing of heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium.

Midstream – NdPr oxide to rare-earth metal, metal to NdFeB alloy, strip casting and alloy processing, hydrogen decrepitation, jet milling, magnetic-field pressing, sintering, heat treatment, grain boundary diffusion, precision machining and surface coating.

Downstream – EV traction motors, wind turbine generators, industrial motors and BLDC fans, defence and aerospace systems, and consumer electronics.

Now, why should we look at this ecosystem?

India's estimated rare-earth permanent magnet demand is projected to reach around 8,220 tonnes annually by 2030.

Against this, the government has introduced a scheme with an outlay of ₹7,280 crore to establish 6,000 TPA of integrated sintered NdFeB magnet manufacturing capacity.

So, even if the entire proposed capacity comes up, it would still be below the projected domestic demand. This leaves room for additional domestic capacity, provided the economics and execution work.

But setting up magnet manufacturing facilities is only one part of the requirement.

Building this ecosystem will require several specialised capabilities, processes and equipment.

This is where the second order opportunities come in.

These include:

- Rare-earth metal production
- Specialised alloy manufacturing and strip casting
- Powder processing and precision equipment
- Hydrogen handling and inert-gas systems
- Magnetic-field pressing
- Vacuum furnaces, sintering and heat treatment
- Grain boundary diffusion
- Precision machining and surface coating
- Testing, inspection and qualification

There will also be requirements for specialised process chemicals, industrial gases, solvent extraction, industrial automation, process control, maintenance and magnet recycling.

But if you look at the entire chain, NdPr oxide availability is one of the important upstream dependencies.

For the proposed 6,000 TPA magnet capacity, the estimated NdPr oxide requirement is around 2,000 tonnes annually.

The government's scheme identifies up to 500 TPA of assured supply from IREL for selected beneficiaries.

So, additional sourcing and processing capabilities will be important if India wants to scale domestic production.

And this is not the only constraint. India will also need capabilities in oxide-to-metal conversion, alloy manufacturing, specialised processing equipment and customer qualification.

This is where I think the opportunity could emerge.

It may be in NdPr oxide-to-metal conversion, rare-earth alloy manufacturing or integrated sintered magnet manufacturing.

These are the capabilities India is specifically trying to establish.

There are already some interesting developments in this direction.

#AshviniRareEarth has established a pilot plant for NdPr metal production, #PGTech is working on molten salt electrolysis and #ARCI has established a pilot facility covering the process from strip-cast alloy to finished sintered magnets.

The companies that can be studied here include #Midwest, #20Microns, #MegathermInduction, #Electrotherm, #MIDHANI, #PTCIndustries, #PermanentMagnets and #Thermax.

We should also track IREL, NFTDC, ARCI, Ashvini Rare Earth, PG Tech and PolyProtic Chemicals for their roles in developing upstream and midstream capabilities.

However, their exposure is different.

Some are directly involved in magnet manufacturing or have participated in the manufacturing scheme. Others have capabilities in metallurgy, equipment, materials or downstream magnetic products that could potentially become relevant as the ecosystem develops.

The important thing is to understand where the spending will happen, which capabilities will be difficult to build and which companies can actually capture that spending as this ecosystem develops.

Wipro +0.6% · HCLTech +2.6% · TCS +2.8% · Tech Mahindra +7.2% · Persistent +20.8%

HCLTech's CEO puts AI-led price deflation at 2–3% a year, and TCS's CEO says 10–15% of productivity gains are passed back to clients.

The key question is whether this is a one-time reset or a 2–3% drag every year. A one-off cut is a bad year. A recurring drag changes what the business is worth, and that is why TCS trades at about 16.9x earnings, down from 30.6x.

There is an upside. AI work earns 7–10 points more margin, according to HCLTech, and it added 32 bp to HCLTech's Q2 margin. TCS's AI revenue is at a $3.1 bn annual run rate. But much of it replaces older work rather than adding to it.

Our test for turning positive on large-cap IT: growth back above 5% for several quarters. That hasn't happened yet. The specialists (Persistent, Coforge, eClerx) are still compounding.

NCL organised a One Day Special Training Programme for Contractual/HoE Supervisors and Workmen of NCL on Thursday at CETI, Singrauli.

The programme aimed at strengthening the safety awareness, statutory compliance, and leadership capabilities of contractual supervisors working in the opencast mines of NCL.

The training covered a wide range of critical topics, including Common Safety Lapses in Opencast Mines & Preventive Strategies, Safe OB Dumping Practices & Slope Stability in Opencast Mine, Safe Haul Road Design, Maintenance & Traffic Discipline between Heavy Motor Vehicles (HMVs) and Light Motor Vehicles (LMVs), Leadership in Safety Creating a Zero-Harm Mining Culture: Statutory responsibilities of supervisors and managers, effective implementation and enforcement of SOPs and SMPs, safety performance monitoring and KPI setting, Behaviour-Based Safety (BBS), incident reporting and investigation, corrective actions, and the role of supervisors in promoting discipline and fostering a proactive safety culture etc.

Around 38 participants from all  Areas/Units of NCL attended the programme. The sessions were conducted by in-house faculties, who shared practical insights and best practices relating to safe mining operations.

दिनांक 19.11.2026 को कोयला भवन मुख्यालय में बीसीसीएल के राजभाषा विभाग द्वारा राजभाषा हिंदी के प्रगामी प्रयोग एवं संशोधित तिमाही प्रगति प्रतिवेदन के प्रारूप पर एक दिवसीय कार्यशाला-सह-प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम का आयोजन किया गया।

कार्यशाला में मुख्यालय के विभिन्न विभागों के अधिकारी-कर्मियों, राजभाषा प्रभारियों, नोडल हिंदी अधिकारियों एवं हिंदी कैडर के कर्मियों ने भाग लिया। प्रशिक्षण के दौरान राजभाषा नीति, राजभाषा अधिनियम, 1963, धारा 3(3) के अनुपालन तथा तिमाही प्रगति प्रतिवेदन के नवीनतम प्रारूप में किए गए संशोधनों की विस्तृत जानकारी दी गई।

कार्यशाला के दौरान संशोधित प्रारूप के अनुरूप प्रतिवेदन तैयार करने, हिंदी में पत्राचार एवं टिप्पण लेखन तथा राजभाषा संबंधी निर्धारित प्रावधानों के प्रभावी अनुपालन पर व्यावहारिक मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करने के साथ-साथ प्रतिभागियों की जिज्ञासाओं का समाधान भी किया गया।

Agree on the diagnosis. The harder truth is India will keep playing catch-up at home while Indians build great companies wherever the ecosystem lets them.
India-born founders have started 96 US unicorns, more than any other country. 

Talent was never the problem.
If Indian corporates won't fund moonshots, they could at least buy them. 

Palo Alto Networks, led by India-born Nikesh Arora, has done 25+ deals: CyberArk ($25B), Chronosphere ($3.35B), and this week Applied Compute ($4.5B), a startup founded in 2025 by ex-OpenAI researchers. He paid in stock for a thesis: every enterprise will need to train and run its own models securely.

In 2021, Arora said Palo Alto wouldn't compete in identity. Four years later, he paid $25B for CyberArk, an identity company. The best acquirers change their thesis when the market changes. Ours rarely form one.
To be fair, Indian companies are buying abroad again: Sun Pharma–Organon ($11.75B), Tata Motors–Iveco (€3.8B), Coforge–Encora ($2.35B). But look at what they buy: mature revenue, mostly paid in cash. Nobody in India pays billions for a two-year-old team betting on where tech goes next.

In consumer tech, we flinched. Zomato bought Urbanspoon in 2015, shut it in five months and went home. Byju's bought Epic and Tynker in the US, then collapsed.
R&D sits at ~0.84% of GDP. Our boards hire CEOs who say "yes sir," not ones who place bets.

Having led M&A for 15+ companies globally, I see Indian corporates sitting under the apple tree waiting for a perfect fruit to fall. It won't.

The custom-software era is ending. The next wave rewards whoever builds or buys first. If we do neither, we'll keep exporting founders instead of products.

9/n | My Stance

Over a favourable multi-year cycle, I believe INDO-MIM has the potential to deliver ~25-30% CAGR in sales.

But I am not ready to initiate a fresh position at current valuations.

As I always say,
- growth rates in manufacturing businesses can surprise intermittently,
- but sustaining extraordinary growth consistently is always a challenge.

💠 At ~12x FY27 P/S, the risk-to-reward isn't favorable enough for my capital allocation preferences.

⚠️ DYDD & DYOR

8/n | Growth Through Adjacencies

Industrial gas turbines, data centre power infrastructure, humanoids, private satellites, electronics, aerospace, medical devices...

INDO-MIM doesn't necessarily need to re-invent itself to participate in these emerging themes.

It can leverage its existing niche engineering capabilities, expand its SKU portfolio and deepen customer relationships.

A mature manufacturing platform participating in emerging industries.

That's what excites me about this business.

7/n | Efficiency

INDO-MIM is already a relatively efficient business.

H1 FY27:

▪️ EBITDA margin: 32%
▪️ PAT margin: 18.2%
▪️ ROCE: 36.5%

▪️ OP/NP Ratio : ~1.8x

There is scope for incremental efficiency through capacity utilisation, backward integration and subsidiary turnarounds.

But over the longer term, I would rather build my expectations around parallel growth in the top line and bottom line than assume perpetual margin expansion.

6/n | Metal Powders & Inventory

🍀 One of the strengths of INDO-MIM lies in its metallurgy and metal powder capabilities.

💠 Backward integration into stainless steel powders is already in place.

Upcoming iron powder capacity:
▪️ 3,000 tonnes annually
▪️ 1,500-2,000 tonnes for captive requirements

▪️ Surplus capacity can be for external sales

While some inventory holding is inherent to the business, WIP and finishing operations deserve closer attention.

🚨 Inventory days increased from 340 to 441 YoY.

🟡 Management intends to reduce this by ~75 days by FY27-end.

3/n | Track Programs, Not Just Sectors

INDO-MIM operates with 6,000–6,500 SKUs

- manufacturing around 1,000–1,200 different components every month.

In aerospace alone, the company intends to add at least 400 components to its existing portfolio of ~1,200.

▪️ From the concall, what I infer is that tracking individual programs, tooling orders and their conversion into commercial production is more meaningful than merely tracking sectoral tailwinds.

💠 The real growth lies in winning more parts per customer, more programs per customer and more customers per capability.

🚨🔥 MAHANADI COALFIELDS IPO: COAL INDIA’S CASH MACHINE IS GOING PUBLIC! 🔥🚨

India’s largest single coal producer has entered the IPO market, but the grey market is surprisingly cold.

Here is the complete breakdown 👇

🏢 Company: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd
💰 Price band: ₹129 to ₹136
📦 Lot size: 110 shares
💵 Minimum investment: ₹14,960
📅 Closing date: 23 November
📊 Issue size: Approximately ₹9,001 crore
🗓 Expected listing: 27 November

This is a 100% Offer for Sale.

Coal India is selling around 66.18 crore shares, representing a 10% stake. Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any money from the IPO. The proceeds will go to Coal India.

⛏️ WHY IS MCL IMPORTANT?

Mahanadi Coalfields produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26.

That represents:

🔹 21% of India’s domestic coal production
🔹 28.4% of Coal India’s total production
🔹 Nearly 34% of Coal India’s consolidated profit

It operates primarily in Odisha’s Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields and has audited coal reserves of approximately 9,840 million tonnes.

At the current production rate, those reserves could last around 45 years.

📈 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE

FY24:

Revenue: ₹31,634 crore
PAT: ₹11,842 crore

FY25:

Revenue: ₹31,353 crore
PAT: ₹10,825 crore

FY26:

Revenue: ₹30,550 crore
Operating EBITDA: ₹12,735 crore
PAT: ₹10,698 crore

Revenue and profit have declined for two consecutive years, but H1 FY27 showed improvement.

H1 FY27 revenue increased 9.3% to ₹16,093 crore, while PAT increased 6.7% to ₹4,881 crore.

💪 THE BIG STRENGTHS

✅ India’s largest single coal producer
✅ Around 45 years of reserve life
✅ Nearly debt-free balance sheet
✅ Cash and investments of approximately ₹20,290 crore
✅ FY26 return on net worth of 53.8%
✅ Low-cost, highly mechanised mining operations
✅ Around 99.8% of production comes from cheaper opencast mines
✅ Long-term agreements provide demand visibility

💸 THE DIVIDEND ANGLE

MCL paid dividends of approximately ₹7,650 crore in FY26, equivalent to roughly ₹11.6 per share.

At the upper IPO price of ₹136, that represents a historical dividend yield of around 8.5%.

That is probably the biggest attraction here.

This looks more like a high-dividend PSU play than a high-growth story.

⚖️ VALUATION

At ₹136, MCL will have a market capitalisation of approximately ₹90,010 crore.

FY26 P/E: Around 8.4x
Cash-adjusted EV/EBITDA: Around 5.5x

The valuation looks reasonable considering its margins, cash position and return ratios, but it is not a screaming bargain compared with Coal India.

⚠️ THE RISKS

❌ Revenue and PAT have declined for two consecutive years
❌ 97% of product sales come from non-coking coal
❌ Power producers contribute around 69% of coal sales
❌ Top 10 customers generate approximately 56% of revenue
❌ Coal India controls most pricing and capital-allocation decisions
❌ MCL has delayed receivables from government power utilities
❌ Environmental clearances, land acquisition and railway capacity can restrict growth
❌ Renewable energy creates a long-term structural risk for coal demand
❌ Possible mineral-levy exposure and regulatory claims remain significant
❌ Coal India may sell more shares later to meet public-shareholding requirements

📉 GMP AND SUBSCRIPTION

Current GMP: Around ₹3.10

Estimated listing price: Approximately ₹139.10
Potential listing gain: Around 2.3%
Estimated profit on one lot: Only around ₹341

Early Day 1 subscription:

Overall: 0.04x
Retail: 0.06x
QIB: 0.00x

This is only an early snapshot. Large IPOs frequently receive most institutional and HNI bids near the closing date.

🎯 ALLOTMENT CHANCE

At the current 0.06x retail subscription, demand is below the available retail quota. If it remained undersubscribed until closing, every valid retail applicant should ordinarily receive an allotment.

But calculating a final allotment probability this early is meaningless because the subscription can change sharply during the final hours.

🔥 MY TAKE

For listing gains, the setup currently looks weak. A ₹3 GMP on a ₹136 issue suggests the grey market is expecting a flat or modest debut.

For long-term income investors, the story is more interesting: huge reserves, strong cash flows, almost no debt, excellent return ratios and a historical dividend yield near 8.5%.

The biggest question is whether that dividend is enough compensation for stagnant earnings, government control and the long-term transition away from coal.

This is a cash-generating PSU giant, but it should be evaluated as an income stock rather than a growth rocket.

How do you sustain a multi-decade infra boom without overloading the public balance sheet?
₹2.9 lakh crore set to be unlocked in FY27, a ~50% jump over FY26. ✅️

₹16.72 lakh crore five-year pipeline across 12 sectors under NMP 2.0 . 
 - incl. ₹5.8 lakh crore in direct private investment.  ✅️

Asset monetisation is now a repeatable capex engine.

Instead of stretching sovereign finances for every greenfield project, the Centre is recycling operational brownfield assets,  combining lease/ concession revenues with committed PPP private capex to free fiscal space for fresh infrastructure. 

After delivering ~₹2 lakh crore (80% of target) in FY26, FY27 is tracking 80–90% of the ₹3.26 lakh crore target.
• Roads (~₹1 lakh crore): NHAI-led via BOT concessions (~₹60,000 crore) and InvITs, still prime paper for domestic and foreign institutions.

• Coal & Mining (~₹80,000 crore): Commercial block auctions, Coal India subsidiary stake dilutions, and mining lease/CL auctions.

Proceeds flow largely to states, partly to the Centre.

• Power & Ports (~₹50,000 crore each): Transmission network leasing in power; PPP berths and terminal concessions at major ports.

• Railways (~₹30,000 crore): Equity dilution in rail PSUs, land monetisation, and freight shed developments.

Build. Operationalise. Monetise. Reinvest.

That’s how you compound national infrastructure without straining fiscal headroom.

இந்த CMPDI கதைய பாருங்க. மார்ச் மாசம் ₹172-க்கு issue பண்ணாங்க. ஆனா ₹160-க்கு தான் லிஸ்ட் ஆச்சு. ஆனா அங்க இருந்து எகிறி 77% வரைக்கும் மேல போயிருக்கு. இப்போ எல்லாத்தையும் இறக்கிட்டு ₹187-ல நிக்குது. அதாவது லிஸ்டிங்ல பயமுறுத்திட்டு அப்புறம் தான் லாபம் கொடுத்திருக்கு. அவங்க Q2 வருமானம் கூட போன வருஷத்தை விட 8% அதிகமாகி ₹593 கோடி வரைக்கும் வந்திருக்கு.

ஆனா BCCL கதை அப்படி இல்ல. ஜனவரில இருந்தே ஒரு மாதிரி மந்தமா தான் இருக்கு. Q2-ல நஷ்டத்துல இருந்து மீண்டு வந்து லாபம் பார்த்தாலும் கூட இன்வெஸ்டர்ஸ்க்கு இது மேல பெரிய நம்பிக்கை வரல போல. ₹19 கோடி லாபம் பார்த்த Q4-க்கு அப்புறம் இப்போ தான் கொஞ்சம் மூச்சு விடுறாங்க. ஆனா செம செல்லிங் பிரஷர்ல இருக்கு.

இந்த ரெண்டுக்கும் நடுவுல தான் இப்போ Mahanadi Coalfields ₹5,012 கோடி திரட்ட வராங்க. இது முழுசா OFS தான். அதாவது மொத்த பணமும் ஷேர் விக்கிறவங்களுக்கு தான் போகும். விலை ₹129-ல இருந்து ₹136 வரைக்கும் வச்சிருக்காங்க. சப்ஸிடரி நிறுவனங்கள் லிஸ்ட் ஆன உடனே கலக்கும்னு நினைச்சா இப்போ நிலைமை வேற மாதிரி இருக்கு. லிஸ்டிங் அன்னைக்கு அடி வாங்குன CMPDI இப்போ மேல இருக்கு, ஆனா BCCL திணறுது. நீங்க எதை நம்பி அப்ளை பண்ணுவீங்க?

Largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India (set up in 1992)  
Contributes ~21% to India’s total coal production  
Operates in Odisha’s Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields  
Estimated reserves: 9,840.3 million tonnes (as of April 2026)  
17 mines (14 opencast + 3 underground) | Produced 218.3 MT in FY26  
Sells mainly via long-term FSAs (~82% of revenue) and e-auctions to power, cement and sponge iron players

Strong volume base with room for mine expansions

Post-IPO P/E ~8.4x on FY26 earnings (~9.2x on annualised H1 FY27)  
Trades at a modest premium to Coal India (7.8x) and NMDC (8.2x), reflecting leadership position and high margins

Morning.

The Fed minutes are the whole story. The October FOMC record landed Wednesday and read more hawkish than the hold itself suggested. Almost all participants thought further increases would be needed to get inflation back to 2%, and a couple said more than 25 basis points could deserve consideration in December if the inflation data stays unfriendly. CME FedWatch now puts roughly 95% odds on a December hike. The US 10-year sits near 5.05%.

That is why the commodity complex is on the floor. Gold fell about 3.5% to $3,730 an ounce, a 14-month low. COMEX silver dropped 3.5% to $45.79, a one-year low. Copper is at a five-month low, aluminium at 2026 lows. Higher-for-longer US rates, a firmer dollar and soft China demand is a poor mix for anything priced in dollars and dug out of the ground.

Crude is the exception, and that is the uncomfortable part. Brent January futures are at $92.45, up 1.1%, even after WTI fell 3.7% Wednesday to $82.85. Blame the Strait of Hormuz, where tanker attacks are at record levels and are cancelling out rising Gulf export volumes. Crude in the low nineties with the rupee at 93.44 is the combination India least wants.

Our tape felt it Wednesday. Nifty closed 25,227.95, down 0.63%, with Nifty Metal the worst sector at -2.46%. Titan fell 4.97% as the weakest Nifty 50 name, purely on gold, and Kalyan Jewellers was off more than 4%. PSU Bank was the only green sector and SBI led the index, up 2.3%. GIFT Nifty is at 25,164 this morning, down about 76 points.

Three names that moved on real news. Fairfax exited its entire 13.64% stake in IIFL Finance, about Rs 3,454 crore at Rs 617, and the stock ran as much as 6.5% to Rs 678, which says the overhang mattered more than the discount. Caplin Point fell 7.7% after the US FDA classified its Gummidipoondi plant as Official Action Indicated. Ashoka Buildcon jumped as much as 10% on being declared L-1 for a Rs 1,465 crore NHAI package.

Three things to watch. Whether the metals and jewellery complex finds a floor, because that is the December hike trade expressing itself on our screens. Brent, since crude firming while the dollar firms is the worst available mix for India. And Mahanadi Coalfields, which opens today as a pure offer for sale by Coal India, alongside anything SEBI says about that unconfirmed report on capping margin-funded purchases.

More after the close.
